subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 3: Grammar – going to and will
outcomes: Use going to for plans you decided before.
Use will for quick decisions at the time of speaking.
Write about your weekend plans with going to.

tf.s: We use going to for plans we decided before.
tf.why: Yes, going to is for plans.

tf.s: We use will for decisions we make at the time of speaking.
tf.why: Yes, will is for quick decisions.

tf.s: I will to take an umbrella is correct.
tf.why: No to after will: I will take an umbrella.

tf.s: The short form of I will is I'll.
The negative of I'm going to visit London is I'm not going to visit London.
We bought the tickets. We will visit London is the best choice.
tf.why: It is a plan, so: We are going to visit London.

tf.s: Both going to and will can talk about the future.
Won't is the short form of will not.
She are going to visit Muscat is correct.
tf.why: We say She is going to …

tf.s: We use going to only for things that happened yesterday.
tf.why: Going to is for the future, not the past.

boxes.q: The phone is ringing. I ___ answer it.
I'm thirsty. – I ___ get you some water.
boxes.why: This is a quick offer, so will.

boxes.q: We ___ visit the mountains for the holidays. (plan)
She ___ visit Muscat this year. (negative plan)
This bag is very heavy! – I ___ help you carry it.
boxes.why: You offer help at that moment.

o: It's cold. I'll close the window.
I'm going to visit my aunt on Saturday.
We're going to fly to London next month.
boxes.why: You decide when you feel cold.

o: I'm going to play football on Friday.
I'm hungry. I'll make a sandwich.
It's raining. I'll take an umbrella.

boxes.q: Correct: I will to take an umbrella.
Complete: I ___ (take) a small bag, too. (decided now)

mcq.q: When do we use going to?
o: for decisions at the time of speaking
for decisions at the time of speaking
for plans we made last week

mcq.q: Which is the correct question form?
o: Are you going to visit London?
You are going to visit London?
Do you going to visit London?
Are you go to visit London?

mcq.q: We bought the tickets. We ___ visit London.
Make it negative: I'm going to visit London.
o: I'm not going to visit London.
I'm going not to visit London.
I don't going to visit London.
I won't going to visit London.

mcq.q: Your friend says: I'm hungry! What do you say?
o: I'm going to make you a sandwich last week.
I made you a sandwich tomorrow.
I will to make you a sandwich.

mcq.q: Why does Frank say I'll take one about the umbrella?
o: He decides when Majid says he doesn't have one.
He is talking about the past.
mcq.why: It is a decision at the time of speaking.

mcq.q: Which pair shows one plan and one quick decision?
o: I'm going to visit Salalah in the summer. It's hot – I'll take my sunhat.
I'll visit Salalah. I'll take my sunhat.
I'm going to visit Salalah. I'm going to visit Nizwa.
I visited Salalah. I took my sunhat.
mcq.why: First a plan, then a quick decision.

mcq.q: Ali says: I'm going to take a pillow on the bus trip. Sami answers: Good idea! I'll take one too. Why does Sami use will?
o: He planned it a week ago.
mcq.why: Sami's idea comes as he speaks.
